catalog: A study of the fundamentals of writing computer programs and problem-solving, using structured and object-oriented techniques. Intended for future majors and minors in Computer Science and minors in Game Development. This course uses C#.

goals.detail: knowledge of a basic computer system architecture.
a problem solving methodology and apply it to writing programs in C#.
an understanding of the basic C# language concepts.
your ability to use a C# editor and debugger.

assess.name: Quizzes
assess.description: At the end of each week, a short in-class quiz on the prior week's reading and concepts.

assess.name: Progress Reports
assess.description: Weekly written update on project status: what was attempted, what works, what doesn't, what's next.

assess.name: Presentation 1: The Pitch
assess.description: Students pitch their semester project: what it is, why it interests them, and which C# concepts they expect to use.

assess.name: Presentation 2: The Progress
assess.description: Students demonstrate working C# code for at least one core feature and explain design decisions made so far.

assess.name: Presentation 3: The Final Form
assess.description: Full project demonstration, code walkthrough, and oral exam. Questions may cover any part of the code.
